answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to accumulate a basalt-solid proof-of-service history: useful work recorded on-ledger over time, weighted so that a freshly spun fake with zero history cannot whisper trades into the shared pool at all. Real reputations behave like opal — they diffract, with service in one domain echoed into others through independent peer attestations, making fakes expensive to forge and cheap to expose.
